audits.claim: The audit endpoint adds an undocumented, untested administrator-only pagination flag and duplicates its paginate call.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22-25 declares only event and actor, while lines 70-82 read optimized_pagination directly and select the new paginator for superusers or globally privileged members. Lines 76-90 repeat the same request, queryset, ordering and serialization arguments in both branches. Searching the checkout tests finds no optimized_pagination or OptimizedCursorPaginator coverage, and the supplied diff adds no endpoint tests; these are maintainability and coverage concerns rather than an independently established runtime defect.

audits.claim: The new 1000-span eviction silently removes old spans and leaves max_segment_spans unused.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197-199 stores payloads with end_timestamp_precise scores, and src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62-64 removes the lowest scores whenever the merged set exceeds 1000. The script returns no eviction count at line 72, and buffer.py:237-279 consumes only redirect/queue/root metadata and emits no eviction metric; buffer.py:449 now loads retained spans without the deleted count-exceeded check. The max_segment_spans constructor argument remains assigned at buffer.py:150-158 but has no remaining enforcement. This confirms lost observability and stale configuration, but truncation itself is the implemented eviction policy, so the comment does not establish that retaining only 1000 spans is unintended.

audits.claim: Reducing redirect traversal from 10000 to 1000 can attach a late span to an intermediate key and split its segment.
audits.evidence: Submit single-span batches s0(parent=s1), s1(parent=s2), through s1002(parent=s1003) for one project/trace before expiry: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:195-220 writes each parent key and invokes the script, whose src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:40 records successive redirects without compressing earlier ones. A later span t(parent=s0) follows only 1001 edges in the inclusive loop at add-buffer.lua:30-38 and stops at s1001 although the live segment is at s1003. Lines 45 and 51-54 then move t from parent key s0 into intermediate key s1001, and buffer.py:258-259 queues that intermediate key separately from s1003. Flushing uses each key's span ID as segment_id at buffer.py:370-393, so t is emitted as a separate segment instead of joining s1003; the old 10000 bound would resolve this chain. The 1000-payload eviction does not bound redirect depth because add-buffer.lua:63 only removes sorted-set members, not redirect hash entries.

audits.claim: ZUNIONSTORE's default SUM can inflate a redelivered payload's timestamp and make eviction keep the wrong spans.
audits.evidence: For a single trace, first deliver A(parent=B), then B(parent=R), in separate batches: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:195-220 and src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:40-48 move A into R's set and record B -> R. Redelivering identical A writes it again under B with its original timestamp at buffer.py:197-199; add-buffer.lua:30-38 resolves B to R and lines 51-54 union B into R without an AGGREGATE override. Because A is present in both sets, default SUM doubles its score, rather than retaining its end_timestamp_precise. Once more than 1000 members are present, add-buffer.lua:62-64 can evict a genuinely newer span while retaining the inflated older A, violating the timestamp-based retention order introduced by this PR.

audits.claim: The PR adds no tests for the new eviction threshold, ordering, merging, or optimized audit pagination.
audits.evidence: The supplied diff only adds end_timestamp_precise arguments to existing buffer tests, and tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:115-522 covers small trees, cross-project parents and rebalance rather than exceeding 1000 spans. Its added timestamp values are identical, so those tests cannot assert which timestamp is evicted by src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62-64. No checkout test references optimized_pagination or OptimizedCursorPaginator either. This is a confirmed missing-test concern, not itself a demonstrated production failure.

audits.claim: A span missing end_timestamp_precise would raise KeyError and abort process_batch, but whether such spans are valid is unconfirmed.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:129-147 directly indexes val["end_timestamp_precise"] before calling buffer.process_spans, so an object with trace_id, span_id and project_id but no timestamp would abort that batch. The cast at factory.py:134 is only a type annotation, but SpanEvent is imported from sentry_kafka_schemas at line 14, whose implementation/schema is not supplied in this checkout; requirements-frozen.txt:126 pins that external package to 1.3.6. Existing downstream code already requires the same timestamp in src/sentry/spans/consumers/process_segments/enrichment.py:160-162, and the updated ingest fixtures contain it. Thus the conditional exception is clear, but the allowed repository evidence does not establish a valid producer/schema path that omits this field.
